brief.scope:
Owner work order, 2026-09-05: deliver a command that starts a new interactive conductor session, selects codex/claude/grok by parameter, and forwards harness CLI arguments intact. Routine work must never pause for manual approval. Safeguards must enforce a declared boundary against destructive actions; do not equate disabling prompts with protection. Root conducts; workers investigate and produce artifacts through ops/bin/dispatch.sh only.
Plan a bounded contract before code. Reuse the lane and installed CLIs; measure behavior and dependencies. Define permission profiles, protected assets, refusals, argument conflicts, startup context/handoff, and limits. No blanket claim of preventing all harm. Preserve main checkout, existing sessions/configuration, master ownership, and retained branches. No automatic forge ruleset changes. Produce a contract/plan with acceptance cases and proposed files for independent tests and review. No implementation.

findings.claim: Harness versions on this host are unmeasured: claude --version, codex --version, grok --version and gh --version were each refused by the harness permission layer under this read job. The plan leans on the lane's dated flag facts (codex 0.148.0, grok 1.0.5, claude 2026-08-28); PATH shows codex 0.153.4 installed, later than the measured version. The proposed probe verb (slice 3) is what closes this; a start refuses class freshness until it runs.

Whether Claude honours the tracked deny rules and PreToolUse hooks under its prompt-skipping permission mode is unmeasured; if it does not, the Claude unattended profile's boundary is the git-native hooks only, containment stays policy, and the profile remains unproven (refusal profile-unproven) so sessions start attended, which pauses. The owner's two rules then conflict on Claude and the owner rules.

laneconf.py closure scans only .py and .sh sources under ops/ and .claude/, so the proposed git hooks (extensionless files pre-push and reference-transaction) reading RELEASE_BRANCH and TRUNK_BRANCH would be undeclared reads invisible to the closure check; slice 2 must give them a scanned shape or extend the reader.

Codex interactive network access inside workspace-write and its config key are unmeasured; a conductor session needs gh and git push, so the codex unattended profile may have to choose danger-full-access with the git hooks as the only boundary, recorded as such.
The term-wall pattern is gitignored configuration and a CI variable; whether any name proposed here trips it could not be looked at. The first PR's CI is the only oracle.

The self-hosted runner's PATH and hook state were not measured; ci.yml prepends only ~/.local/bin and never runs install.sh. Tests must plant stub harness binaries and scratch clones; a test that skips when a real binary is absent is an unreachable arm read as a pass.

The main checkout's working tree has no harness-independent guard: git offers no pre-checkout hook and a read-only .git directory would break every worktree. The plan declares the gap (Claude-only matrix row plus a start record) rather than claiming coverage.
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'The main checkout belongs to nobody' CONTRIB.md

findings.claim: The snapshot's .git directory is writable by this uid: .git/index mtime is 54 seconds after .git/HEAD mtime, so git refreshed the index during this job. Read-only holds by policy and read-role settlement, not by filesystem mode, for claude and grok read jobs.
Starting the harness by exec leaves the session's end unrecorded unless the profile opts into a wrapper; the owner may prefer the wrapper for every session, a one-line data change.

envelope.note: Plan written to out/PLAN.md (56 KB): a bounded contract for ops/bin/conduct.sh over ops/conductor/tools/conduct.py with profiles as data (prompting half and boundary half, boundary-absent refused), protected assets with per-layer binding and declared gaps, a harness-independent git-native boundary (pre-push and reference-transaction hooks keyed on CONDUCT_SESSION), argument-conflict rules over per-harness reserved flags, a startup brief from onboard.py, a two-arm probe verb with freshness and profile-unproven refusals, five slices (four S, one M with two named S buckets) each with tests named and why red at the ref, a first-run walkthrough with 15 assumption lines each measured or a refusal, calibration rows, and tab-separated machine lines. Could not look: harness and gh versions, network, env, the job directory above snapshot/, and a direct write probe into .git (each refused by the harness under this read job); all declared in the plan. The snapshot was not edited; the only writes were out/PLAN.md. The in/ directory was empty.
